Largest portfolio holding Insmed to be acquired by Sanofi
IBT notes the announcement today that Insmed has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by Sanofi for a total consideration of $41 billion.

Insmed is a global biopharmaceutical company focused on developing therapies for respiratory diseases. The company has two commercialised medicines, Brinsupri and Arikayce, a phase 3 clinical program in treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP), and several earlier stage programs across immunology and rare diseases.

Under the terms of the agreement, Insmed shareholders will receive $175 per share in cash at closing, representing a premium of approximately 46% to Insmed’s closing share price on 18 November, prior to media reports of a possible acquisition. As at close of business on Friday 20 November, Insmed was IBT’s largest holding, representing 8.54% of IBT’s Net Asset Value, as included in IBT’s daily NAV update on Monday 23 November.
Commenting on the news, Ailsa Craig and Marek Poszepczynski, portfolio managers of IBT, said:

“This is a genuine mega deal that builds on another strong year of M&A activity for biotech - the largest deal in the sector since Pfizer acquired Seagen for $43bn in 2023, also IBT’s largest position at the time. The pharmaceutical sector is going through a golden age for deals, with a towering patent cliff driving a buying binge of biotech companies, often at significant premiums.

“Sanofi’s acquisition of Insmed is a great result for IBT, on its own covering our dividend payment to shareholders twice over. Insmed represents the tenth acquisition in our portfolio in 2026, surpassing the nine deals we saw in 2025, and cumulatively around 30% of our entire portfolio acquired this year, in NAV terms.”
The updated valuation of IBT’s holding in Insmed will be included in IBT’s NAV as at close of business on 23 November, to be reported in the usual way later today.
